questions.question: In a toaster, the heating wire glows red because __________.

options.text: It resists the current and gets hot.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It resists the current and gets hot**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The heating wire in a toaster glows red due to the **Heating Effect of Electric Current**, also known as **Joule Heating**. This phenomenon occurs when an electric current passes through a conductor with significant resistance, converting **electrical energy** into **thermal energy**.
 
• **Resistance** is the property of a material that opposes the flow of electrons. When electrons collide with the ions/atoms of the conductor (the heating wire), they transfer kinetic energy, which manifests as **heat**. *Hence, statement 4 is correct.*
 
• If the wire had **zero resistance**, it would be a **superconductor**. In such a case, no heat would be generated because there is no opposition to the current flow (H = I²Rt, where R=0 leads to H=0). *Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.*
 
• Heating elements must have a **high melting point** to ensure they do not melt or deform while operating at temperatures high enough to glow red (typically above **500°C** to **1000°C**). A **low melting point** is a characteristic of a **fuse wire**, not a heating element. *Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.*
 
• While the **current** flowing through the toaster is substantial, the "glowing red" is specifically the result of that current meeting high **resistance**. High current alone in a low-resistance thick copper wire would not cause it to glow red under normal household conditions. *Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Nichrome:** The most common material used for heating wires in toasters and space heaters is **Nichrome**, which is an alloy consisting of approximately **80% Nickel** and **20% Chromium**. 
 
• **High Resistivity:** Nichrome is chosen because it has relatively **high electrical resistivity** compared to copper or aluminum, allowing it to generate significant heat in a compact space.
 
• **Oxidation Resistance:** When heated to high temperatures, Nichrome forms a protective layer of **chromium oxide** on its surface, which prevents the wire from further **oxidation** and breaking down in the open air.
 
• **Incandescence:** The "red glow" is a form of **incandescence**. As the temperature of the wire increases, it begins to emit **electromagnetic radiation** in the visible spectrum, starting with **long-wavelength red light**.
 
• **Applications:** Apart from toasters, this principle is utilized in **electric irons**, **geysers**, **hair dryers**, and **room heaters**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Joule's Law of Heating:** The heat produced (**H**) in a conductor is directly proportional to the **square of the current** (**I²**), the **resistance** (**R**), and the **time** (**t**) for which the current flows. The formula is expressed as **H = I²Rt**.
 
• **Material Comparison:**
 
 
• **Heating Element:** High resistance and **High melting point** (e.g., **Nichrome**, melting point ~**1400°C**).
 
• **Fuse Wire:** High resistance and **Low melting point** (e.g., **Tin-Lead alloy**, melting point ~**183°C** to **230°C**) to protect circuits by melting during a power surge.
 
• **Bulb Filament:** Extremely high melting point (e.g., **Tungsten**, melting point ~**3422°C**) to withstand temperatures high enough to emit white light.

questions.question: A sealed syringe containing air is pressed from one end while keeping the other end closed. What is the most likely outcome of this action in terms of the state of air inside the syringe?

options.text: The temperature of air inside drops significantly
The air escapes completely from the syringe
The volume of air increases and pressure decreases
The volume of air decreases and its pressure increases

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The volume of air decreases and its pressure increases**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When a **sealed syringe** is pressed, the plunger moves inward, which directly reduces the physical space available for the air trapped inside. This results in a **decrease in volume**.
 
• According to **Boyle's Law**, discovered by **Robert Boyle** in **1662**, for a fixed amount of gas at a **constant temperature**, the pressure and volume are inversely proportional. This means as the **volume decreases**, the **pressure increases** simultaneously. ***Hence, option 4 is correct.***
 
• Air is a mixture of gases, and gases possess high **compressibility** because of the large **intermolecular spaces** between their particles. In a **sealed system**, pressing the plunger forces these particles closer together.
 
• The temperature of the air would not drop significantly; in fact, if compressed rapidly, the **temperature** might increase slightly due to the work done on the gas molecules. ***Hence, option 1 is incorrect.***
 
• Because the syringe is **closed at the other end** and properly **sealed**, the mass of the air remains constant, and it cannot escape the container. ***Hence, option 2 is incorrect.***
 
• The action of pressing the plunger is a physical reduction of the container's size, which contradicts the idea of an increase in volume. ***Hence, option 3 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Kinetic Molecular Theory:** This theory explains that gas **pressure** is caused by the frequent collisions of gas molecules against the walls of their container. When the **volume** is reduced, the molecules have less space to travel and hit the walls more often, thus increasing the measured pressure.
 
• **States of Matter:** Unlike **solids** and **liquids**, which have fixed volumes and are almost incompressible, **gases** do not have a fixed shape or volume and can be easily compressed into smaller containers.
 
• **Applications:** This principle is utilized in various **pneumatic systems**, **bicycle pumps**, **medical syringes**, and even in the functioning of **internal combustion engines** where the air-fuel mixture is compressed by a piston before ignition.
 
• **Isothermal vs. Adiabatic:** If the compression happens slowly enough for heat to exchange with the surroundings, it is an **isothermal process** (constant temperature). If it happens very fast, it is an **adiabatic process**, where the internal energy and temperature of the air increase.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Ideal Gas Law:** The relationship between these variables is summarized by the formula **PV = nRT**, where **P** is pressure, **V** is volume, **n** is the number of moles, **R** is the universal gas constant, and **T** is temperature.
 
• **Direct and Inverse Proportions:** In science, it is vital to distinguish between these. In a syringe, the **inverse proportion** between **P and V** is a fundamental concept taught in **General Science** and **Physics** to explain the behavior of matter.
 
• **Standard Units:** Pressure is often measured in **Pascals (Pa)** or **Atmospheres (atm)**, while volume in the context of a syringe is usually measured in **milliliters (ml)** or **cubic centimeters (cm³)**.

questions.concept: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.question: Which of the following symbols is used for the element phosphorus as per the rules for atomic symbols?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**P**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The chemical symbol for the element **Phosphorus** is **P**. It is derived from the first letter of its name, following the standard **IUPAC** (International Union of Pure and Applied Chemistry) nomenclature where symbols for many elements consist of a single **capitalized letter**.
 
• **Phosphorus** is a chemical element with the **atomic number 15**. It belongs to **Group 15** of the periodic table, which is also known as the **Pnictogens**.
 
• The name phosphorus originates from the **Greek** word **phosphoros**, which means "**bringing light**" or "**light-bearer**." This name was given due to its property of glowing in the dark when exposed to oxygen.
 
• In its elemental form, it is highly reactive and is never found as a free element on **Earth**. It is essential for life, appearing in **DNA**, **RNA**, **ATP**, and the **phospholipids** that form all cell membranes.
 
• The correct symbol is not **Ph**, **Ps**, or **Pr**. While **Pr** is a valid atomic symbol, it represents **Praseodymium**, not phosphorus. **Ph** is frequently used in organic chemistry as a shorthand for the **phenyl group**, but it is not an atomic symbol for a single element.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Discovery and History**:
 
 
• Phosphorus was discovered by the **German alchemist Hennig Brand** in the **year 1669**. He isolated it from **human urine**, making it the first element to be discovered that was not known since ancient times.
 
 
 
• **Allotropes of Phosphorus**:
 
 
• **White Phosphorus**: A waxy, dangerous solid that is **highly flammable** and toxic. It glows in the dark (**chemiluminescence**).
 
• **Red Phosphorus**: More stable than white phosphorus and is used in the striking surface of **matchboxes**. It is non-toxic compared to the white variety.
 
• **Black Phosphorus**: The most stable form and is produced by heating white phosphorus under high **pressure**. It resembles **graphite** in its structure and properties.
 
 
 
• **Physical and Chemical Characteristics**:
 
 
• **Atomic Mass**: Approximately **30.974 u**.
 
• **Location**: It is situated in **Period 3** and **p-block** of the **Periodic Table**.
 
• **State at Room Temperature**: It exists as a **solid**.
 
 
 
• **Industrial and Biological Uses**:
 
 
• The largest industrial use of phosphorus compounds is in the production of **fertilizers** (such as **phosphates**) to replace the phosphorus that plants remove from the soil.
 
• It is also used in the manufacture of **detergents**, **pesticides**, **steel**, and **safety matches**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Rules for Atomic Symbols**:
 
 
• According to the **Dalton’s** and later **Berzelius's** suggestions, symbols of elements are represented by the first letter (in **Uppercase**) or the first and second letter (second being **lowercase**) of the element's name in **English**, **Latin**, or **Greek**.
 
• Examples: **Hydrogen (H)**, **Carbon (C)**, **Oxygen (O)**, and **Iron (Fe** from Latin Ferrum).
 
 
 
• **Comparison of the Options**:
 
 
• **Ph**: Not an element symbol; used for **Phenyl** functional groups.
 
• **P**: Correct symbol for **Phosphorus**.
 
• **Ps**: Not a standard atomic symbol for a naturally occurring element.
 
• **Pr**: Symbol for **Praseodymium**, a rare earth metal with **atomic number 59**.
 
 
 
• **Phosphate Cycle**: In the **environment**, phosphorus is most commonly found as the **phosphate ion (PO4³⁻)**. It is a critical limiting **nutrient** in many ecosystems, especially aquatic ones.

questions.question: Which connective tissue is known for supporting internal organs?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Areolar tissue**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Areolar tissue** is the most widely distributed **connective tissue** in the animal body. It acts as a supporting and packing tissue between most of the organs.
 
• It is found located between the **skin** and **muscles**, around **blood vessels** and **nerves**, and in the **bone marrow**.
 
• The primary functions of **areolar tissue** include filling the **space inside the organs**, providing support to **internal organs**, and assisting in the **repair of tissues** after injury. ***Hence, the correct answer is Areolar tissue.***
 
• This tissue consists of a **semifluid ground substance** (matrix) that contains three types of cells: **fibroblasts**, **macrophages**, and **mast cells**.
 
• It also contains two types of protein fibers: **white collagen fibers**, which provide tensile strength, and **yellow elastic fibers** (elastin), which allow for flexibility and recoil.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Squamous epithelium**: 
 
 
• Unlike areolar tissue, this is an **epithelial tissue**, not a connective tissue. It is composed of a single thin layer of **flattened cells** with irregular boundaries.
 
• It is primarily found in the walls of **blood vessels** and the **alveoli** (air sacs) of the lungs.
 
• Its main function is to form a **diffusion boundary** for the exchange of gases and nutrients.
 
 
 
• **Tendon**: 
 
 
• **Tendons** are a type of **dense regular connective tissue** characterized by great strength but limited flexibility.
 
• Their specific function is to connect **skeletal muscles to bones**, facilitating movement of the skeleton when muscles contract.
 
 
 
• **Ligament**: 
 
 
• **Ligaments** are also **dense connective tissues**, but they are highly **elastic** and possess significant strength.
 
• They contain very little matrix and serve the crucial role of connecting **one bone to another bone** at joints, maintaining structural stability.
 
 
 
• **Adipose Tissue**: 
 
 
• This is another type of **loose connective tissue** located mainly beneath the **skin** and between **internal organs**.
 
• The cells of this tissue (**adipocytes**) are specialized to **store fats**, which acts as an **insulator** and an energy reservoir for the body.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Connective Tissues** are categorized into three main types: **Loose connective tissue** (e.g., Areolar and Adipose), **Dense connective tissue** (e.g., Tendons and Ligaments), and **Specialized connective tissue** (e.g., Cartilage, Bone, and Blood).
 
• The **matrix** is a non-living material secreted by the cells of the connective tissue, which can be **fluid, jelly-like, or solid** depending on the tissue's function.
 
• In **Areolar tissue**, the loose arrangement of fibers allows the tissue to be flexible yet strong enough to bind different tissue types together, such as connecting the **epithelial tissue** to the underlying structures.
 
• **Fibroblasts** within the areolar tissue are the cells responsible for secreting the **fibers** (collagen and elastin) and the **polysaccharides** that make up the ground substance.
</ul

questions.question: How does the space between particles change from solid to gas?

options.text: Solids and gases always have equal spacing
The space remains unchanged during the change in states of matter
The space increases as matter changes from solid to gas
The space decreases as matter changes from solid to gas

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The space increases as matter changes from solid to gas**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to the **Kinetic Molecular Theory**, all matter is made of **particles** that are in constant motion, and the **space** between these particles determines the **state of matter**.
 
• In a **solid**, particles are **tightly packed** in a fixed, regular **lattice structure** with very little **intermolecular space** between them. 
 
• As a substance transitions to a **liquid** state, the particles gain **energy** and move further apart, creating moderate **gaps** that allow them to slide past each other.
 
• In the **gaseous** state, particles have high **kinetic energy** and are **widely separated**, occupying much larger **volumes** compared to their solid or liquid forms.
 
• The **intermolecular distance** is greatest in **gases** and smallest in **solids**. ***Hence, the statement that the space increases as matter changes from solid to gas is correct.***
 
• **Statement 1**: Solids and gases always have equal spacing. ***This statement is incorrect*** as **gases** have significantly more **void space** than **solids**.
 
• **Statement 2**: The space remains unchanged during the change in states of matter. ***This statement is incorrect*** because **phase changes** (like **melting** or **evaporation**) are fundamentally defined by the change in **particle arrangement** and **distance**.
 
• **Statement 4**: The space decreases as matter changes from solid to gas. ***This statement is incorrect*** as this describes **condensation** or **freezing** (gas to liquid/solid), not the transition to a gas.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Intermolecular Forces**: These are the **attractive forces** between molecules. They are **strongest** in **solids**, keeping the particles in fixed positions, and **weakest** (almost negligible) in **gases**, allowing particles to move **independently**.
 
• **Kinetic Energy and Temperature**: The transition from **solid to gas** usually occurs by increasing **temperature**. Adding **heat** increases the **kinetic energy** of the particles, allowing them to overcome **intermolecular attractions** and increase their **separation**.
 
• **Compressibility**: Because **gases** have large **intermolecular spaces**, they are highly **compressible**. **Solids** have very little **empty space**, making them virtually **incompressible**.
 
• **Density**: For most substances, **density** is highest in the **solid** phase and lowest in the **gas** phase because the same **mass** occupies a much larger **volume** in the gaseous state due to increased **particle spacing**.
 
• **Shape and Volume**: **Solids** have a **definite shape** and **fixed volume** due to lack of space between particles. **Gases** have **no definite shape** or **volume**, expanding to fill the entire **container** they occupy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Sublimation**: This is the **direct transition** of a substance from **solid to gas** without passing through the **liquid phase** (e.g., **dry ice** or **naphthalene**), which results in a massive and rapid increase in **intermolecular space**.
 
• **Thermal Expansion**: Even within a single state, increasing **temperature** generally causes a slight increase in **intermolecular distance**, leading to the **expansion** of the material.
 
• **Pressure Effects**: Increasing **pressure** on a **gas** reduces the **space** between particles, which can eventually force a **phase change** back into a **liquid** state through **liquefaction**.
</ul

questions.question: A scientist observed a multicellular organism undergoing reproduction. Which of the following methods would the plant NOT be using?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Binary Fission**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Binary Fission** is a primary method of **asexual reproduction** typically observed in **unicellular organisms**, where a single cell divides into two approximately equal and **genetically identical daughter cells**.
 
• Since the scientist is observing a **multicellular organism**, it possesses complex structures and specialized tissues that cannot simply split into two through cellular fission to reproduce the entire organism. ***Hence, the statement that the organism would NOT use binary fission is correct.***
 
• **Multicellular organisms**, particularly plants, utilize more complex mechanisms for **asexual reproduction** such as **budding**, **fragmentation**, and **vegetative propagation**, which involve the growth of new tissues from specialized regions.
 
• In **Binary Fission**, the **genetic material (DNA)** replicates and the **cytoplasm** divides, a process common in **prokaryotes** like **bacteria** and some **eukaryotic protists** like **Amoeba**.
 
• The other options—**Budding**, **Fragmentation**, and **Vegetative Propagation**—are all viable methods for various multicellular plants and simple multicellular animals.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Budding:**
 
 
• In this process, a small **outgrowth or bud** develops on the parent body due to repeated **cell division** at one specific site.
 
• These buds develop into tiny individuals and, when fully mature, **detach** from the parent body to become new independent individuals.
 
• **Examples** include **Hydra** (a multicellular animal) and **Yeast** (a unicellular fungus).
 
 
 
• **Fragmentation:**
 
 
• This occurs when a **multicellular organism** simply breaks up into smaller pieces upon maturation.
 
• Each piece, or **fragment**, grows into a new complete individual through **regeneration** of missing parts.
 
• **Examples** include filamentous algae like **Spirogyra** and some flatworms like **Planaria**.
 
 
 
• **Vegetative Propagation:**
 
 
• This is a form of **asexual reproduction** in plants where new plants are produced from **vegetative parts** such as **roots**, **stems**, and **leaves** rather than seeds.
 
• Methods include **tubers** (potato), **runners** (strawberry), and **leaf notches** (**Bryophyllum**).
 
• It allows for the rapid production of **genetically uniform** offspring and is widely used in **horticulture**.
 
 
 
• **Binary Fission Details:**
 
 
• It is the simplest form of reproduction. In **Amoeba**, the division can take place in any plane, whereas in **Leishmania** (which causes **Kala-azar**), it occurs in a definite orientation in relation to whip-like structures.
 
• Because it involves the division of a **single cell** into two, it is biologically impossible for a complex **multicellular plant** to undergo this process as a whole.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Complexity and Reproduction:** As organisms become more complex (multicellular), their **reproductive strategies** shift from simple cell division to processes involving **specialized reproductive cells** or tissues.
 
• **Asexual vs. Sexual:** All methods mentioned in the options are types of **asexual reproduction**, meaning they do not involve the fusion of **gametes** and result in offspring that are **clones** of the parent.
 
• **Environmental Adaptation:** **Vegetative propagation** and **fragmentation** are often advantageous in stable environments where the parent's traits are already well-suited for survival.

questions.question: What is the general name of the reaction between an acid and a base?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Neutralisation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• A **Neutralisation** reaction is a specific type of chemical reaction where an **acid** and a **base** react with each other to produce **salt** and **water**.
 
• In aqueous solutions, this reaction occurs when **H+ ions** (hydrogen ions) from the acid combine with **OH- ions** (hydroxyl ions) from the base to form **H2O** (water) molecules.
 
• The general chemical equation representing this process is: **Acid + Base → Salt + Water**. For example, the reaction between **Hydrochloric acid (HCl)** and **Sodium hydroxide (NaOH)** produces **Sodium chloride (NaCl)** and water.
 
• Neutralisation reactions are generally **exothermic** in nature, meaning they involve the **evolution of heat** during the process.
 
• The resulting **pH** of the solution depends on the strength of the reactants; a reaction between a **strong acid** and a **strong base** typically results in a solution with a **pH of 7** (neutral)

questions.question: A boy lifts an object above his head by exerting a force. Which of the following works is negative?

options.text: Work done by the force of gravity
Work done by the applied force

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Work done by the force of gravity**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Work** is defined in physics as the product of the **force** applied to an object and the **displacement** of the object in the direction of that force. The formula is **W = F d cos(theta)**, where **theta** is the angle between the force and displacement vectors.
 
• When a boy lifts an object above his head, the **displacement** of the object is in the **upward direction**.
 
• The **force of gravity** (weight) acts on the object vertically **downward** toward the center of the Earth.
 
• Because the displacement is **upward** and the force of gravity is **downward**, the angle **theta** between them is **180 degrees**.
 
• The value of **cos(180) is -1**; therefore, the work done by the **force of gravity** is **negative**. *Hence, option 1 is the correct answer.*
 
• Conversely, the **applied force** exerted by the boy is in the **upward direction**, the same as the displacement. This means the angle is **0 degrees**, and since **cos(0) is 1**, the **work done by the boy** is **positive**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Positive Work:** This occurs when the force and the displacement are in the **same direction** (angle between **0 and 90 degrees**). A common example is a horse pulling a cart or a person pushing a car forward.
 
• **Zero Work:** Work is zero if the force is **perpendicular** to the displacement (**90 degrees**) or if there is **no displacement**. For example, a person holding a heavy box stationary or a satellite moving in a **circular orbit** (where centripetal force is perpendicular to velocity) does no work.
 
• **SI Unit of Work:** The standard unit is the **Joule (J)**. One Joule is the work done when a force of **1 Newton** moves an object through a distance of **1 meter**.
 
• **Nature of Work:** Work is a **scalar quantity**, meaning it only has magnitude and no specific direction in space, even though force and displacement are **vectors**.
 
• **Dimensions:** The dimensional formula for work is **[M1 L2 T-2]**, which is the same as the dimensions of **energy**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Work-Energy Theorem:** This theorem states that the **net work** done on an object is equal to the **change in its kinetic energy**. When gravity does negative work, it often results in an increase in the object's **potential energy**.

questions.question: Which property enables carbon to form long chains?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Catenation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Catenation** is the unique property of an element to form **covalent bonds** with other atoms of the same element, resulting in the formation of **long chains**, branched structures, or rings.
 
• Among all known elements, **Carbon** exhibits the maximum tendency for catenation due to the high strength and stability of the **Carbon-Carbon (C-C) bond**.
 
• This property allows carbon to form an almost infinite variety of molecules, ranging from simple **hydrocarbons** to complex biological macromolecules like **DNA** and **proteins**.
 
• The ability to form **single, double, and triple bonds** between carbon atoms further enhances the structural diversity enabled by catenation.
 
• It is because of catenation and **tetravalency** that carbon forms such a large number of compounds, leading to the dedicated branch of science known as **Organic Chemistry**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Tetravalency**:
 
 
• Carbon has **four valence electrons** in its outermost shell, allowing it to form four covalent bonds with other atoms.
 
• This characteristic enables carbon to link with a wide variety of other elements like **hydrogen, oxygen, nitrogen, and sulfur**, as well as other carbon atoms.
 
 
 
• **Isomerism**:
 
 
• This is the phenomenon where compounds have the same **molecular formula** but different **structural arrangements** or spatial orientations.
 
• Since catenation allows for different chain lengths and branching, **isomers** are very common in organic compounds, contributing to their vast chemical variety.
 
 
 
• **Polymerisation**:
 
 
• This is a chemical process in which small units called **monomers** join together to form a very large molecule called a **polymer**.
 
• While catenation is the inherent atomic property, **polymerisation** is the process used to create materials like **plastics (polyethene)**, **rubber**, and **nylon**.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Silicon**:
 
 
• **Silicon** also shows catenation properties but to a much lesser extent than carbon.
 
• Silicon can form chains with hydrogen (silanes) up to about **7 or 8 atoms**, but these compounds are highly reactive and unstable because the **Si-Si bond** is significantly weaker than the **C-C bond**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Bond Energy**: The stability of carbon chains is attributed to the high bond enthalpy of the **C-C bond**, which is approximately **348 kJ/mol**. In contrast, the **Si-Si bond** energy is only about **222 kJ/mol**.
 
• **Atomic Size**: Carbon is a **small-sized atom**, which allows the nucleus to hold the shared pair of electrons in the covalent bond more tightly, leading to a **strong and stable bond**.
 
• **Allotropes of Carbon**: Catenation is also responsible for the different forms of carbon, such as **Diamond** (3D network), **Graphite** (layered hexagonal sheets), and **Fullerenes** (spherical cages like **C60**).
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following is the correct unit of average speed in SI system?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**m/s**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Average speed** is defined as the **total distance** traveled by an object divided by the **total time** taken to cover that distance.
 
• In the **International System of Units (SI)**, which was established in **1960**, the standard unit for **length (distance)** is the **meter (m)** and the standard unit for **time** is the **second (s)**.
 
• By using the formula **Speed = Distance / Time**, the derived SI unit becomes **meters per second**, mathematically expressed as **m/s** or **m s⁻¹**.
 
• **Option 1 (km/h²)**: This is not a recognized standard unit for speed or average speed in the SI system, though km/h is a common metric unit for speed. ***Hence, this statement is incorrect.***
 
• **Option 2 (m/s²)**: This is the **SI unit of acceleration**, which measures the rate of change of velocity over time. ***Hence, this statement is incorrect.***
 
• **Option 3 (s/m²)**: This unit does not represent any standard physical quantity in classical mechanics. ***Hence, this statement is incorrect.***
 
• **Option 4 (m/s)**: This is the correct **SI unit** for both instantaneous speed and **average speed**. ***Hence, this statement is correct.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Scalar vs Vector**: Speed is a **scalar quantity** because it possesses only **magnitude** and no direction. **Velocity**, which is the displacement divided by time, is a **vector quantity** as it includes both magnitude and direction.
 
• **Measuring Instruments**: In automobiles, the **speedometer** is used to measure the **instantaneous speed** of the vehicle at any given moment, while the **odometer** records the **total distance** traveled.
 
• **Unit Conversion**: In daily life, speed is often expressed in **kilometers per hour (km/h)**. To convert **1 km/h to m/s**, we multiply by **5/18** (since 1000m / 3600s = 5/18). For example, **36 km/h** is equal to **10 m/s**.
 
• **Dimensional Formula**: The **dimensional formula** for speed is **[M⁰ L¹ T⁻¹]**, indicating it is independent of mass (M) and depends on length (L) and time (T).
 
• **Types of Speed**: Apart from average speed, there is **Uniform speed** (covering equal distances in equal intervals of time) and **Variable speed** (covering unequal distances in equal intervals of time).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **CGS System**: In the **Centimetre-Gram-Second (CGS)** system of units, the unit of speed is **centimeter per second (cm/s)**.
 
• **FPS System**: In the **Foot-Pound-Second (FPS)** system, speed is measured in **feet per second (ft/s)**.
 
• **Speed of Light**: The ultimate speed limit in the universe is the **speed of light** in a vacuum, which is approximately **299,792,458 m/s** (often rounded to **3 x 10⁸ m/s**).
 
• **Supersonic Speeds**: Speeds exceeding the speed of sound (approx. **343 m/s** in air) are referred to as **supersonic** and are often measured using **Mach numbers**.

questions.question: A sound wave has a speed of 320 { m/s} . If the wavelength of the wave is 0.4 { m} , what is the frequency of this wave?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**800 Hz**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The relationship between the speed, frequency, and wavelength of a wave is governed by the universal wave equation: **Speed (v) = Frequency (f) × Wavelength (λ)**.
 
• In the given problem, the **speed of the sound wave (v)** is **320 m/s** and the **wavelength (λ)** is **0.4 m**.
 
• To calculate the **frequency (f)**, the formula is rearranged as **f = v / λ**.
 
• By substituting the provided numerical values into the equation: **f = 320 / 0.4**.
 
• The calculation **320 / 0.4** equals **800**. Thus, the **frequency** of the sound wave is **800 Hz**. ***Hence, the correct answer is 800 Hz.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Frequency:**
 
 
• **Frequency** refers to the number of complete **oscillations** or wave cycles that pass a fixed point in **one second**.
 
• The **SI unit** of frequency is the **Hertz (Hz)**, named after the physicist **Heinrich Hertz**. One Hertz is equivalent to **one cycle per second**.
 
 
 
• **Wavelength:**
 
 
• **Wavelength** is the spatial period of a periodic wave—the distance over which the wave's shape repeats.
 
• In **longitudinal waves** like sound, it is the distance between the centers of two consecutive **compressions** or two consecutive **rarefactions**. It is measured in **meters (m)**.
 
 
 
• **Nature of Sound Waves:**
 
 
• Sound is a **mechanical wave**, meaning it requires a **medium** (solid, liquid, or gas) to travel. It cannot propagate through a **vacuum**.
 
• It is also a **longitudinal wave**, where the particles of the medium vibrate **parallel** to the direction of energy transport.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Human Audibility:** The standard **audible range** for humans is between **20 Hz and 20,000 Hz (20 kHz)**. Since **800 Hz** falls within this range, it is an **audible sound** to the human ear.
 
• **Pitch and Frequency:** The **pitch** of a sound is directly proportional to its **frequency**. A wave with a higher frequency is perceived as having a **higher pitch** (shrill), while a lower frequency is perceived as a **lower pitch** (grave).
 
• **Speed of Sound in Air:** The speed of sound is not constant; it varies with **temperature** and **humidity**. For example, at **0 degrees Celsius**, the speed is approximately **331 m/s**, whereas at **20 degrees Celsius**, it increases to about **343 m/s**.
 
• **Medium Density:** Sound travels fastest in **solids** (due to high elasticity and density), slower in **liquids**, and slowest in **gases**. In steel, the speed can reach approximately **5960 m/s**.

questions.question: Which structure in *Rhizopus *is directly involved in the process of reproduction through spore formation?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sporangia**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Rhizopus** is a genus of saprophytic fungi, commonly known as **bread mold**, which belongs to the phylum **Zygomycota**.
 
• The **Sporangia** (singular: **sporangium**) are the spherical, sac-like structures specifically responsible for **asexual reproduction** through the production of **spores**. ***Hence, statement 2 is correct.***
 
• These structures develop at the tips of specialized upright hyphae known as **sporangiophores**.
 
• Inside the **sporangium**, the protoplasm undergoes cleavage to form thousands of minute, multinucleate, and non-motile **sporangiospores**.
 
• When the **spores** mature, the outer wall of the **sporangium** ruptures due to internal pressure or environmental factors, dispersing the **spores** into the air to colonize new substrates.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Hyphae**:
 
 
• These are the individual, thread-like filaments that make up the body of the fungus. In **Rhizopus**, the **hyphae** are **coenocytic**, meaning they are continuous tubes filled with multinucleated cytoplasm without **septa** (cross-walls).
 
• While they form the structural basis, they are not the direct site of spore formation. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **Mycelium**:
 
 
• The **mycelium** refers to the entire collective network or mass of **hyphae** that constitutes the vegetative part of the fungus.
 
• It is responsible for nutrient absorption and spreading across the **substrate** (like **bread** or **fruit**). ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **Rhizoids**:
 
 
• **Rhizoids** are root-like, branching **hyphae** that grow downward into the food source.
 
• Their primary **functions** include anchoring the fungus to the **substrate** and secreting **digestive enzymes** to absorb organic nutrients. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **Stolons**:
 
 
• These are horizontal **hyphae** that grow along the surface of the **substrate**, connecting different clusters of **rhizoids** and **sporangiophores**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Asexual Reproduction**: This is the most common method of reproduction in **Rhizopus**, occurring rapidly under favorable conditions of **moisture** and **temperature** (typically **25°C to 30°C**).
 
• **Sexual Reproduction**: While **sporangia** handle asexual cycles, **Rhizopus** can also undergo sexual reproduction through the fusion of two compatible **gametangia**, leading to the formation of a thick-walled **zygospore**.
 
• **Columella**: This is the central sterile portion found inside the **sporangium**. It plays a role in nutrient exchange for the developing **spores**.
 
• **Economic Importance**: Some species like **Rhizopus stolonifer** cause food spoilage, while others like **Rhizopus oryzae** are used in the **industrial production** of **lactic acid** and **cortisone**.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is true about weight and mass?

options.text: Both mass and weight change on the Moon
Only mass changes on the Moon
Neither mass nor weight changes on the Moon
Only weight changes on the Moon

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only weight changes on the Moon**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mass** is defined as the **total quantity of matter** contained in an object. It is an **intrinsic property** of the body and remains **constant** regardless of the location in the universe, whether on Earth, the Moon, or in deep space.
 
• **Weight** is the **gravitational force** exerted on an object by a celestial body. It is calculated using the formula **W = m × g**, where **m** is mass and **g** is the **acceleration due to gravity**.
 
• The **acceleration due to gravity** on the **Moon** is approximately **1.62 m/s²**, which is about **1/6th** (or **16.6%**) of the gravity on **Earth** (**9.8 m/s²**). Since **g** changes, the **weight** of an object will change when moved to the Moon.
 
• The statement "Both mass and weight change on the Moon" is incorrect because **mass** is a **scalar quantity** that does not depend on gravity. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• The statement "Only mass changes on the Moon" is incorrect because **mass** remains **invariant**, while **weight** is the property that actually fluctuates. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• The statement "Neither mass nor weight changes on the Moon" is incorrect because while **mass** is constant, the **gravitational pull** of the Moon is significantly weaker than Earth's, causing **weight** to decrease. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• The statement "Only weight changes on the Moon" is correct because an object's **matter** stays the same, but the **force of gravity** acting upon it decreases to **1/6th** of its Earth value. ***Hence, statement 4 is correct.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Detailed Comparison of Mass and Weight:**
 
 
• **Measurement Units**: The **SI unit** of **mass** is the **kilogram (kg)**, whereas the **SI unit** of **weight** is the **Newton (N)**, as it is a measure of **force**.
 
• **Nature of Quantity**: **Mass** is a **scalar quantity** (it has only magnitude), while **weight** is a **vector quantity** because it acts in a specific direction (towards the center of the gravity source).
 
• **Measuring Instruments**: **Mass** is typically measured using a **physical balance** or **beam balance**, while **weight** is measured using a **spring balance**.
 
 
 
• **Gravity on Different Celestial Bodies:**
 
 
• On **Jupiter**, which has a much higher mass than Earth, the **acceleration due to gravity** is about **24.79 m/s²**. Consequently, an object's **weight** would increase by more than **2.5 times**, even though its **mass** remains exactly the same.
 
• In a state of **free fall** or in **outer space** far from any planet, an object can become **weightless** (Weight = 0), but it will still possess its original **mass**.
 
 
 
• **Practical Example:**
 
 
• If a person has a **mass** of **60 kg** on Earth, their **weight** on Earth would be **60 kg × 9.8 m/s² = 588 Newtons**.
 
• On the **Moon**, that same person’s **mass** remains **60 kg**, but their **weight** becomes **60 kg × 1.62 m/s² ≈ 98 Newtons**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Inertia**: **Mass** is often described as a measure of **inertia**, which is the resistance of an object to any change in its state of **motion**. The higher the **mass**, the higher the **inertia**.
 
• **Variation of 'g' on Earth**: Even on **Earth**, **weight** can vary slightly because the Earth is an **oblate spheroid**. Gravity is slightly stronger at the **poles** (where you are closer to the center) and slightly weaker at the **equator**.
 
• **Newton's Law of Universal Gravitation**: This law states that every point **mass** attracts every other point **mass** by a **force** acting along the line intersecting both points. This **force** is what we perceive as **weight**.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an olfactory indicator?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Litmus**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Olfactory indicators** are substances whose **odor** or **smell** changes depending on whether they are mixed with an **acidic** or **basic** solution.
 
• **Onion** is a well-known olfactory indicator. When treated with a base like **sodium hydroxide (NaOH)**, the characteristic sharp smell of onion cannot be detected. however, its smell does not vanish when treated with an acid. ***Hence, it is an olfactory indicator.***
 
• **Vanilla essence** has a characteristic pleasant smell. If we add a few drops of dilute **Hydrochloric acid (HCl)**, the smell persists, but if we add dilute **NaOH**, the smell of vanilla vanishes. ***Hence, it is an olfactory indicator.***
 
• **Clove oil** also acts as an olfactory indicator. Its distinct smell changes or disappears in the presence of a **base**, while it remains detectable in **acidic** conditions. ***Hence, it is an olfactory indicator.***
 
• **Litmus** is a **natural indicator** but it is a **visual indicator** rather than an olfactory one. It changes its **color** in different media; it turns **red** in acidic solutions and **blue** in basic solutions. It does not rely on a change in smell for detection. ***Hence, it is NOT an olfactory indicator and is the correct answer.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Natural Indicators:**
 
 
• These are indicators obtained from natural sources like plants.
 
• **Litmus** is extracted from **Lichens** (a symbiotic relationship between algae and fungi). It is the most commonly used indicator in laboratories.
 
• **Turmeric** is another natural indicator. It remains **yellow** in acidic solutions but turns **reddish-brown** in basic solutions (often seen when soap, which is basic, touches a turmeric stain).
 
 
 
• **Synthetic Indicators:**
 
 
• These are laboratory-synthesized chemical indicators used to test acidity or alkalinity.
 
• **Phenolphthalein** is a popular synthetic indicator that remains **colorless** in acidic solutions and turns **pink** in basic solutions.
 
• **Methyl Orange** turns **red** in acidic media and **yellow** in basic media.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Olfactory Indicators:**
 
 
• Olfactory indicators are particularly useful for **visually impaired** students in chemistry laboratories, as they can identify the nature of a substance (acid or base) through the sense of **smell** rather than sight.
 
 
 
• **pH Scale:**
 
 
• The **pH scale** was introduced by **S.P.L. Sorensen** in **1909** to measure the concentration of hydrogen ions in a solution.
 
• The scale ranges from **0 to 14**, where **7** is neutral, values below 7 are **acidic**, and values above 7 are **basic** or alkaline.
 
 
</ul

Concave lens cannot form a real image

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Concave lens cannot form a real image**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• A **concave lens** is also known as a **diverging lens** because it diverges the parallel rays of light incident on it after **refraction**.
 
• For any position of a **real object**, a concave lens always forms a **virtual, erect, and diminished** image.
 
• A **virtual image** is formed when light rays appear to meet at a point but do not actually intersect; therefore, such images **cannot be obtained on a screen**. ***Hence, the student's claim of forming an image on a screen is a fundamental mistake.***
 
• While a concave lens does indeed form **diminished** images, the impossibility of it being **real** (and thus projectable on a screen) is the primary error in the student's observation. <stro

questions.question: The disease-causing pathogens in plants can be transmitted through______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both Soil and Air**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Plant pathogens** are biological agents such as **fungi**, **bacteria**, **viruses**, and **nematodes** that cause diseases in plants, leading to significant agricultural loss worldwide.
 
• **Soil transmission** occurs when pathogens reside in the soil and infect plant roots or the base of the stem. Soil-borne pathogens can survive for long periods in the absence of a host by forming **dormant structures**. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• **Air transmission** involves the movement of pathogen propagules, primarily **spores**, through wind currents. These spores can travel short distances within a field or thousands of miles across continents. ***Hence, statement 3 is correct.***
 
• The transmission of diseases is a complex process where pathogens utilize multiple media, including **water (rain splash/irrigation)**, **insect vectors**, and **contaminated seeds**, but **soil and air** remain the primary environmental pathways for dispersal.
 
• Because pathogens can utilize both the subterranean environment (soil) and the atmosphere (air) to find new hosts, the disease spread is categorized as both **soil-borne** and **air-borne**. ***Hence, the correct answer is Both Soil and Air.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Soil-borne Diseases:**
 
 
• These diseases are often caused by fungi like **Fusarium**, **Rhizoctonia**, and **Pythium**.
 
• They typically cause **root rot**, **damping-off**, and **vascular wilts**.
 
• Pathogens in the soil can remain viable for **5 to 10 years** or more in the form of **chlamydospores** or **sclerotia**.
 
• **Prevention**: Techniques like **crop rotation** and **soil solarization** are used to manage these pathogens.
 
 
 
• **Air-borne Diseases:**
 
 
• Fungal **rusts**, **smuts**, and **mildews** are classic examples of air-borne plant diseases.
 
• **Puccinia graminis** (Wheat Rust) is a famous air-borne pathogen that produces millions of **urediniospores** that are carried by the **wind**.
 
• **Environmental factors** like **relative humidity** and **wind velocity** play a crucial role in the successful dispersal and germination of air-borne spores.
 
• **Late Blight of Potato**, caused by **Phytophthora infestans**, spread rapidly across **Ireland** in the **1840s** due to air-borne and water-borne transmission.
 
 
 
• **Other Transmission Modes:**
 
 
• **Vector-borne**: Many **plant viruses** (e.g., **Tobacco Mosaic Virus**) are transmitted by insects like **aphids**, **whiteflies**, and **leafhoppers**.
 
• **Seed-borne**: Pathogens can be carried on the surface of or inside **seeds**, ensuring the disease is present when the plant begins to grow.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Disease Triangle**: For a plant disease to occur, three factors must coincide: a **susceptible host**, a **virulent pathogen**, and a **favorable environment**.
 
• **Impact on Economy**: It is estimated that plant diseases reduce global crop yields by approximately **10% to 16%** annually, affecting **food security**.
 
• **Modern Detection**: Farmers now use **spore traps** and **remote sensing** to monitor air-borne pathogens and **DNA-based soil testing** to identify soil-borne threats before planting.
</ul

questions.question: The filament of a light bulb is made up of tungsten, because of its ______.

options.text: High resistance and high melting point
High resistance and low melting point
Low resistance and low melting point
Low resistance and high melting point

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**High resistance and high melting point**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The filament of an incandescent light bulb is made of **Tungsten** (chemical symbol **W**) because it possesses a **high melting point** and **high resistance**.
 
• **High Melting Point**: Tungsten has the highest melting point of all metallic elements, recorded at approximately **3422°C** (**6192°F**). This characteristic is crucial because the filament must reach temperatures above **2000°C** to emit visible light through **incandescence** without melting or deforming.
 
• **High Resistivity**: Tungsten provides significant **electrical resistance**. When an electric current passes through the thin tungsten wire, the **Joule heating effect** (expressed as **Heat = I²Rt**) converts electrical energy into intense thermal energy, causing the filament to glow.
 
• **Low Vapor Pressure**: At elevated temperatures, tungsten exhibits a very **low vapor pressure**, which minimizes the rate of **sublimation**. This prevents the filament from thinning too quickly and reduces the darkening of the glass bulb caused by metal deposits.
 
• **Ductility and Strength**: Tungsten is highly **ductile**, meaning it can be drawn into very fine wires. It also maintains great **tensile strength** even at high temperatures, which is necessary for the stability of the coiled filament structure.
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is High resistance and high melting point.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Composition of a Light Bulb**:
 
 
• A standard incandescent bulb consists of a **glass envelope**, a **tungsten filament**, and **contact wires**.
 
• The bulb is typically filled with an **inert gas** such as **Argon** or **Nitrogen** (sometimes **Krypton**) to prevent the **oxidation** of the tungsten filament, which would otherwise burn up instantly in the presence of oxygen.
 
 
 
• **Historical Context**:
 
 
• Early light bulbs used **carbon filaments**, but they had a lower melting point and shorter lifespan. **Tungsten filaments** were introduced around **1904**-**1906**, revolutionizing the lighting industry due to their superior durability and brightness.
 
• The transition to tungsten was significantly advanced by **William Coolidge** in **1910**, who developed a method to make tungsten more **ductile**.
 
 
 
• **Energy Efficiency**:
 
 
• Incandescent bulbs are relatively inefficient compared to modern **LED** (Light Emitting Diode) or **CFL** (Compact Fluorescent Lamp) technology.
 
• Approximately **90% to 95%** of the energy consumed by a tungsten bulb is released as **heat**, while only **5% to 10%** is converted into **visible light**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Tungsten Properties**: It has an **atomic number of 74** and is found in minerals like **Wolframite** and **Scheelite**. Its name "Tungsten" is derived from the Swedish words for **heavy stone**.
 
• **Resistance and Temperature**: The electrical **resistance** of tungsten **increases** as the temperature rises. When the bulb is first switched on, the "cold" resistance is low, leading to a brief **inrush current** before the filament heats up and the resistance stabilizes.
 
• **Evaporation and Life Span**: Over time, even with inert gas, tungsten atoms slowly **evaporate** from the filament. This leads to "hot spots" where the wire becomes thinner, has higher resistance, gets even hotter, and eventually **breaks**, which is why a bulb "burns out."
 
• **Halogen Bulbs**: In a **Halogen lamp**, a small amount of halogen gas (like **Iodine** or **Bromine**) is added. This triggers a **chemical reaction** that returns evaporated tungsten back to the filament, allowing it to operate at higher temperatures and last longer than standard bulbs.
